category_title: Students with SCD engaged in passive, non-academic tasks like stuffing envelopes
minimal_context: The student is sitting in a self-contained high school special education classroom with the goal of completing a generic math worksheet.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright everyone, here is the math worksheet. Please complete all the problems on the front page.

STUDENT: (Sits quietly at the desk, looking down at the worksheet without picking up a pencil or interacting with anyone.)

TUTOR: Make sure you are working on your worksheet.

STUDENT: (Remains seated with no competing behavior, just passively observing the room and not writing anything down.)

TUTOR: Keep trying, you need to finish the same activity as your peers.

STUDENT: (Continues to be a passive observer, staring blankly at the unindividualized worksheet without responding or attempting the task.)

options.A: Terminate the academic demands and remove the math worksheet from the student's desk for a brief period of 10 seconds.
options.B: Implement systematic instruction and provide frequent, effective, and efficient feedback (praise or corrective) on the math worksheet.
options.C: Lower expectations for the student and reduce the task demand, asking them to complete two math problems instead of the whole page.
options.D: Provide a kit comprising assorted coloring sheets, art materials, and crayons as an alternative to the math worksheet.
